Roast Turkey

Served at: Thanksgiving Day (United States) · Christmas Day

Serves 8-10Prep 30 minCook 3 to 4 hours

Roast turkey is a classic centerpiece for Thanksgiving and Christmas dinners in the United States. This traditional dish symbolizes abundance and gratitude, bringing family and friends together around the holiday table.

Ingredients

  • 1 whole turkey (12-14 pounds / 5.5-6.5 kg), thawed if frozen
  • 1/2 cup (115 g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 2 teaspoons salt
  • 1 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1 teaspoon dried thyme
  • 1 teaspoon dried rosemary
  • 1 teaspoon dried sage
  • 1 large onion, quartered
  • 1 lemon, halved
  • 4 garlic cloves, smashed
  • 2 cups (480 ml) low-sodium chicken broth or water
  • Fresh herbs (such as rosemary, thyme, and sage) for stuffing the cavity (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C).
  2. Remove the turkey giblets and pat the turkey dry with paper towels.
  3. In a small bowl, mix the softened butter with salt, pepper, thyme, rosemary, and sage.
  4. Loosen the skin of the turkey breast gently with your fingers and spread half of the butter mixture under the skin.
  5. Rub the remaining butter mixture all over the outside of the turkey.
  6. Stuff the cavity with onion, lemon, garlic, and fresh herbs if using.
  7. Place the turkey breast side up on a rack in a roasting pan.
  8. Pour the chicken broth or water into the bottom of the pan to keep the environment moist.
  9. Tent the turkey loosely with aluminum foil to prevent over-browning.
  10. Roast the turkey, basting occasionally with pan juices, for about 13-15 minutes per pound (about 3 to 4 hours), removing the foil during the last 45 minutes to brown the skin.
  11. Check the internal temperature with a meat thermometer; it should read 165°F (74°C) in the thickest part of the thigh.
  12. Remove the turkey from the oven and let it rest for at least 20-30 minutes before carving to allow the juices to redistribute.

Tips

  • For extra crispy skin, pat the turkey dry and let it sit uncovered in the refrigerator for several hours before roasting.
  • Use a meat thermometer to ensure the turkey is cooked safely and avoid overcooking.
  • Save the pan drippings to make a flavorful gravy to serve alongside the turkey.
